claim: Activation and increased numbers of inflammatory macrophages in adipose tissue are deleterious in metabolic diseases.
source: Activation and increased numbers of inflammatory macrophages, in adipose tissue (AT) are deleterious in metabolic diseases.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract without specific supporting data in this manuscript.

claim: AT macrophage accumulation was previously considered to be due to blood infiltration or local proliferation.
source: Up to now, AT macrophages (ATM) accumulation was considered to be due to blood infiltration or local proliferation, although the presence of resident hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells (Lin-/Sca+/c-Kit+; LSK phenotype) in the AT (AT-LSK) has been reported.
evidence: This refers to prior understanding in the field, representing established knowledge before this study.

claim: Resident hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells with LSK phenotype are present in adipose tissue.
source: Up to now, AT macrophages (ATM) accumulation was considered to be due to blood infiltration or local proliferation, although the presence of resident hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells (Lin-/Sca+/c-Kit+; LSK phenotype) in the AT (AT-LSK) has been reported.
evidence: This is stated as previously reported knowledge, supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Some inflammatory ATM that induce metabolic disease originate from resident AT-LSK.
source: By using transplantation of sorted AT-LSK and gain and loss of function studies we show that some of the inflammatory ATM inducing metabolic disease, originate from resident AT-LSK.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data from transplantation and functional studies described in the manuscript.

claim: Transplantation of AT-LSK from HFD mice is sufficient to induce ATM accumulation in control mice.
source: Transplantation of AT-LSK sorted from high fat diet-fed (HFD) mice is sufficient to induce ATM accumulation, and to transfer metabolic disease in control mice.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data from transplantation experiments.

claim: Transplantation of AT-LSK from HFD mice transfers metabolic disease to control mice.
source: Transplantation of AT-LSK sorted from high fat diet-fed (HFD) mice is sufficient to induce ATM accumulation, and to transfer metabolic disease in control mice.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data from transplantation experiments.

claim: Transplantation of control AT-LSK improves AT-inflammation in HFD mice.
source: Conversely, the transplantation of control AT-LSK improves both AT-inflammation and glucose homeostasis in HFD mice.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data from transplantation experiments.

claim: Transplantation of control AT-LSK improves glucose homeostasis in HFD mice.
source: Conversely, the transplantation of control AT-LSK improves both AT-inflammation and glucose homeostasis in HFD mice.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data from transplantation experiments.

claim: Resident AT-LSK are a key point of metabolic disease.
source: Our results clearly demonstrate that resident AT-LSK are one of the key point of metabolic disease, and could thus constitute a new promising therapeutic target to fight against metabolic disease.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: AT-LSK could constitute a new therapeutic target to fight metabolic disease.
source: Our results clearly demonstrate that resident AT-LSK are one of the key point of metabolic disease, and could thus constitute a new promising therapeutic target to fight against metabolic disease.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential therapeutic applications based on the findings.

claim: A critical role of adipose tissue macrophages in the initiation of metabolic inflammation has been documented over the last two decades.
source: Over the last two decades a critical role of adipose tissue macrophages (ATM) in the initiation of the metabolic inflammation, commonly found in highly prevalent chronic diseases such as obesity, has been largely documented (Chawla et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: At the onset of HFD-induced metabolic disease, accumulating ATM exhibit an inflammatory phenotype characterized by CD11c expression.
source: At the onset of high-fat diet (HFD)-induced metabolic disease, accumulating ATM exhibit an inflammatory phenotype characterized by CD11c expression and this contributes to adipocyte dysfunction and insulin resistance (Lumeng et al., 2007; Lumeng et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: CD11c+ ATM contribute to adipocyte dysfunction and insulin resistance.
source: At the onset of high-fat diet (HFD)-induced metabolic disease, accumulating ATM exhibit an inflammatory phenotype characterized by CD11c expression and this contributes to adipocyte dysfunction and insulin resistance (Lumeng et al., 2007; Lumeng et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: An increased number of ATM worsens features of metabolic disease.
source: In addition, an increased number of ATM worsens features of metabolic disease (Hirasaka et al., 2007; Kamei et al., 2006), whereas a reduced number of ATM is associated with a reduced metabolic inflammation and an improved metabolic status (Kanda et al., 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: A reduced number of ATM is associated with reduced metabolic inflammation and improved metabolic status.
source: In addition, an increased number of ATM worsens features of metabolic disease (Hirasaka et al., 2007; Kamei et al., 2006), whereas a reduced number of ATM is associated with a reduced metabolic inflammation and an improved metabolic status (Kanda et al., 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: ATM have beneficial effects in obesity by buffering and processing excessive amounts of lipids.
source: Although most of the literature supports the idea that ATM cause disease, accumulating evidences recently show that these ATM also have beneficial effects in obesity. Different molecular tools such as lipid storage (Aouadi et al., 2014), autophagy (Fitzgibbons and Czech, 2016), or program of lysosomal metabolism (Xu et al., 2013) are used by the ATM to buffer and process excessive amounts of lipids and maintain adipose tissue (AT) homeostasis, in the context of metabolic disease.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: ATM use lipid storage, autophagy, and lysosomal metabolism to maintain AT homeostasis in metabolic disease.
source: Different molecular tools such as lipid storage (Aouadi et al., 2014), autophagy (Fitzgibbons and Czech, 2016), or program of lysosomal metabolism (Xu et al., 2013) are used by the ATM to buffer and process excessive amounts of lipids and maintain adipose tissue (AT) homeostasis, in the context of metabolic disease.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: An acute inflammatory response in AT is essential for adipose remodeling and adipocyte differentiation.
source: In addition, an acute inflammatory response in the AT would be essential for adipose remodeling and adipocyte differentiation, and thus for a healthy AT expansion (Cinti et al., 2005; Wernstedt Asterholm et al., 2014; Ye and McGuinness, 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Macrophages invading AT originate from the bone marrow via blood circulation.
source: It is of common knowledge that macrophages invading the AT originate from the bone marrow (BM) via blood circulation (Weisberg et al., 2003) notably in response to AT inflammation which has been shown to trigger the proliferation of BM hematopoietic progenitors and myelopoiesis, that in turn perpetuate local maladaptive inflammatory response (Nagareddy et al., 2014, 2013; Singer et al., 2014, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: AT inflammation triggers proliferation of BM hematopoietic progenitors and myelopoiesis.
source: It is of common knowledge that macrophages invading the AT originate from the bone marrow (BM) via blood circulation (Weisberg et al., 2003) notably in response to AT inflammation which has been shown to trigger the proliferation of BM hematopoietic progenitors and myelopoiesis, that in turn perpetuate local maladaptive inflammatory response (Nagareddy et al., 2014, 2013; Singer et al., 2014, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: BM-derived myelopoiesis perpetuates local maladaptive inflammatory response in AT.
source: It is of common knowledge that macrophages invading the AT originate from the bone marrow (BM) via blood circulation (Weisberg et al., 2003) notably in response to AT inflammation which has been shown to trigger the proliferation of BM hematopoietic progenitors and myelopoiesis, that in turn perpetuate local maladaptive inflammatory response (Nagareddy et al., 2014, 2013; Singer et al., 2014, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Reduced apoptosis, local proliferation, and reduced migration capacity of resident ATM may lead to their accumulation in obesity.
source: In addition to monocyte recruitment, recent studies suggest a local regulation and proliferation of ATM, independently of BM precursors. Reduced apoptosis, local proliferation, as well as reduced migration capacity of resident ATM may also lead to their accumulation in obesity (Amano et al., 2014; Hill et al., 2015; Ramkhelawon et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: A functional resident hematopoietic stem/progenitor cell population exists in adipose tissue in physiological state.
source: In physiological state, we and others recently demonstrated the presence of a peculiar functional resident hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells (LSK) population in the AT (Han et al., 2010; Poglio et al., 2012, 2010) that can renew innate immune cells and especially macrophages in the AT, via in situ differentiation.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work including the authors' own studies.

claim: AT-LSK can renew innate immune cells and macrophages in AT via in situ differentiation.
source: In physiological state, we and others recently demonstrated the presence of a peculiar functional resident hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells (LSK) population in the AT (Han et al., 2010; Poglio et al., 2012, 2010) that can renew innate immune cells and especially macrophages in the AT, via in situ differentiation.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work including the authors' own studies.

evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1d.

source: Chimeric mice became glucose intolerant as revealed by intraperitoneal glucose tolerance test (ipGTT) (Figure 1d), their fasting glucose and insulin levels were significantly higher from that of normal chow fed mice (Figure 1d and e), and their scAT exhibited insulin resistance as shown by reduced glucose utilization in response to insulin (Figure 1f).
